summary: The state a region shows when it has nothing to show, and why — first run, no results, no access, or a failed fetch.
useWhen: a list, table, panel or route has no content to render
a filter or search returns nothing
the account is not permitted to see what would be here
the request that would have filled the region failed

useInstead.when: content exists and something went wrong beside it
useInstead.why: an Alert sits with the content; an EmptyState replaces it. If there is a table on screen, the message about it is an Alert

useInstead.when: the message is transient and the content is unaffected

title.note: required — it is the region's statement. Name the thing and the situation: "No invoices match these filters", not "No results"

description.note: one or two sentences: what would be here, and what puts it here

action.note: the action that RESOLVES this reason — clearing a filter for no-results, not creating a record

secondaryAction.note: a lower-emphasis escape hatch — "Contact an admin"

icon.note: decorative only, rendered aria-hidden — the title already says what this is

children.note: extra content between the description and the actions

first-run.use: nothing exists yet and the user has never created one
first-run.note: the only reason where a create action is the right primary

no-results.use: records exist; the current filter or query matches none of them
no-results.note: the action is clearing the filter. Offering "Create" here tells a user with 400 records and a typo that their data is gone

no-access.use: records exist and match, but this account may not see them
no-access.note: name the permission or plan. "Nothing here" for a permissions problem sends the user to support with the wrong question

error.use: the request that would have filled the region failed
error.note: the action is a retry. Never a create — offering one over a failed fetch invites a duplicate record

inline.use: inside something that already has a frame — a table body, a card

panel.use: a region of a page. The default

page.use: a whole route with nothing in it

guarantees: the title renders as a real heading, so the region appears in the document outline
the icon is aria-hidden, so a screen reader is not told the same thing twice
requires: a `title` that states the situation, since it is what a screen-reader user hears in place of the missing content
`headingLevel` matching the surrounding outline — h3 is the default, but only the page knows its real level
notes: This is deliberately NOT a live region. An empty state replaces content, so it is what the user reads next rather than something announced over what they are reading — `role="status"` here fires on every keystroke of a filter box. If a flow genuinely needs the announcement, pass `role` yourself.
`headingLevel` takes 2-6 and defaults to 3. It is a number rather than a variant because it is an outline decision, not a visual one — the size prop is what changes how the title looks.
`h1` is not available: an empty state describes a region, and the page's own title belongs to the page. Same call FullCard makes.
Under forced-colors the reason tint is discarded, so the region draws a border to stay distinguishable from the content it replaced.

antiPatterns.dont: using `first-run` for an empty filter result
antiPatterns.why: it is the most common empty-state bug in enterprise software: a user with 400 invoices and a typo in their filter is told they have none, and offered a button to make one

antiPatterns.dont: "No data" or "Nothing found" as the title
antiPatterns.why: it names neither the thing nor the situation, so the user cannot tell whether to create a record, clear a filter, or ask for access

antiPatterns.dont: an EmptyState while the request is still in flight
antiPatterns.why: it asserts the data is absent before anything knows, then contradicts itself a moment later
the fetch failed, so nobody knows whether the record already exists — this is how duplicates get made

antiPatterns.dont: an icon with its own `aria-label` or visible caption
antiPatterns.why: the slot is decorative and the title already carries the meaning; a labelled icon makes it announce twice

antiPatterns.dont: hiding the region entirely when it is empty
antiPatterns.why: a section that vanishes is indistinguishable from one that failed to render, and the user cannot tell that they are looking at everything there is

antiPatterns.dont: an EmptyState above a form nobody has filled in yet
antiPatterns.why: a form's empty state IS its initial state — see the Form pattern. A message saying the form is empty is noise on top of a form that is visibly empty
